shrines.artwork_description: Original iconographic study. Installed images and their adornment require image references.

shrines.label: Vinayaka — Entrance Shrine
shrines.evidence: The temple authority locates this image on the right immediately after entering.
shrines.notes: This is the interior Vinayaka worship image. A smaller Ganesha relief is also above the gateway.
shrines.artwork_description: Sculptural study from the Department’s photo of the silver-covered Vinayaka. Engraving and garland arrangement are approximate.

shrines.label: Anjaneya — Wall Shrine
shrines.evidence: A wall-mounted Anjaneya is described on the right near the flagstaff approach.
shrines.notes: The department also lists Anjaneya in the visitor’s darshan sequence.
shrines.artwork_description: Profile relief study from the Department’s photo of the silver-covered Anjaneya. Fine engraving is approximate.

shrines.label: Nandi — Sanctum Approach
shrines.evidence: The small Nandi inside the main temple faces the goddess’s sanctum.
shrines.notes: The large hill-road monolith belongs to a separate pavilion down the hill.
shrines.artwork_description: Small reclining-bull study. The dimensions and installed ornaments are approximate.

shrines.label: Devi’s Sacred Footprints
shrines.evidence: The temple authority records the goddess’s footprints alongside the flagstaff sequence.
shrines.notes: Worship marks representing the goddess’s feet.
shrines.artwork_description: Symbol study based on the documented identity. The exact carving has not been verified against a close photograph.

shrines.label: Nandini — Inner Door Guardian
shrines.evidence: The authority names Nandini as one of two guardians at the inner entrance.
shrines.notes: Nandini and Kamalini flank the inner approach. Their individual sides have not been verified.
shrines.artwork_description: Original guardian relief study. The exact carving remains unverified.

shrines.label: Kamalini — Inner Door Guardian
shrines.evidence: The authority names Kamalini as one of two guardians at the inner entrance.
shrines.notes: Kamalini and Nandini flank the inner approach. Their individual sides have not been verified.
shrines.artwork_description: Original guardian relief study. The exact carving remains unverified.

shrines.evidence: The Development Authority describes a small Ganesha on the entrance tower doorway.
shrines.notes: A doorway image distinct from the interior Vinayaka shrine.
shrines.artwork_description: Approximate study of the gateway relief.

shrines.label: Dvarapalas — Gopura Doorway
shrines.evidence: The temple authority describes door guardians on both sides of the doorway.
shrines.notes: The visit faces the first of the paired reliefs at the entrance.
shrines.artwork_description: Paired relief silhouettes. Individual identities, attributes and originals require close documentation.

shrines.label: Silver Doorway — Devi Reliefs
shrines.evidence: The temple authority records a silver-plated doorway bearing images of the Goddess in several forms.
shrines.notes: The relief program is represented as a door study, with no unsupported identification of individual panels.
shrines.artwork_description: Sculptural doorway study. Exact panel subjects and their arrangement still need a verified reference.

shrines.label: Gopura Construction Record
shrines.evidence: The Karnataka temple department lists a Kannada inscription about the gopura’s construction. The Development Authority attributes the tower to Krishnaraja Wodeyar III and gives 1827 for his work.
shrines.notes: The Department places the Kannada record on the left of the entry. Its catalogue dates it to the 18th century, while the Development Authority dates the Wodeyar work to 1827. The inscription has not been independently dated or transcribed.
shrines.artwork_description: Reference point on the documented left of the entrance. The exact inscribed surface has not been reproduced.

shrines.label: Bhimeswara Shiva Linga
shrines.evidence: Documented site identity; model details and positions are schematic.
shrines.notes: Ground-floor darshan of Bhimeswara. The single tall pale linga rises into the upper storey, reached by paired stair flights.
